design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (creditor_client_services, category client).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {prerequisite_problems: 1, problems: 2, factor_counts: [6, 5]}. client_ext_invoice_late_charge takes 6 factors, client_ext_past_due_invoice_payoff takes 5; the single edge is value_input.
[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: client_ext_early_termination_charge + book_early_termination_charge_4cc8362c, client_ext_closing_settlement_payment + pay_closing_fee_settlement_180c3708 (closing of an agreement under termination notice). Claimed here: client_ext_invoice_late_charge + assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6 (client_late_charge_assessed) and client_ext_past_due_invoice_payoff + pay_past_due_invoice_8492adb5 (client_fee_payment_received applied to ONE named invoice of an agreement with no termination notice). The two payment policies are disjoint by object (one invoice vs the whole closing balance) and by situation (termination notice on record or not); their prerequisite sentences differ in text and direction (task 0 affirmative 'only after', task 1 negated 'not ... until'). After this task every extended policy is claimed; nothing is reserved.
[Design thesis] Surface goal: 'pay off invoice OV-526061 in full today, myself'. Chain: payoff rule's prerequisite sentence 'A payoff figure for a past-due invoice is not quoted until the invoice carries a late charge for every full calendar month it has stayed unpaid after its late-charge start.' -> ledger: OV-526061 dated 2026-07-07, late-charge start 2026-08-16, two full months ended by 2026-10-16, only the 2026-09-16 charge booked -> late-charge rule (6 factors) -> book 18.17 -> payoff rule (5 factors) -> customer pays 1841.24. Breadth: 71 client ledger rows over Jul 2025-Oct 2026, agreement tier/tenure, flatfee program + purchase entry, legal agreement + 16 matter rows.
[Why a good test] The caller names only the invoice. The agent must read the payoff rule's wait, count full months from the late-charge start (exclusive start, base time gate), book the missing month with a six-factor charge whose inputs span the invoice, the other invoices' late charges in a 12-month window (with a 12-months-and-5-days-old near-miss), the client's flat-fee pack payment record and its legal deposit standing, then quote a payoff whose late-charge inclusion method turns on the charge just booked. Skipping the charge gives 1840.50; reading only computation documents gives 27.55 and 1870.06.
[Problem-tree card] root client_ext_past_due_invoice_payoff (user) <- client_ext_invoice_late_charge (agent); kind value_input, gate late_entering, form state, policy_source above (negated direction: a quote 'is not quoted until' what it waits for stands), condition: one late-charge entry per full month since the late-charge start, latest month included; resolved_by assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6. Four-point test: connective 'not ... until'; waited-on side is a record-visible state (late-charge entries on the invoice) with no action/tool; no code token; scope exactly 'every full calendar month ... after its late-charge start'. Exactly one write of this difficulty books client_late_charge_assessed (the late-charge rule's target tool). False at opening: initial_state.client_ledger.<OV-526061 invoice>.txn_date = 2026-07-07 and the only late charge on it, initial_state.client_ledger.<lc>.txn_date = 2026-09-16. Flip: booking 18.17 dated 2026-10-20 -> latest charge 18.17, late_entering 15.19 -> 18.17. Deletion sensitivity (run): payoff 1840.50 instead of 1841.24. Order: step 9 then step 11. Persona never mentions late charges or prior bookings; tools validate nothing.
[Base-invariant card] Late-charge subject is governed by client_evt_fee_billing; its time gate late_charge_start_reached applies: anchor the invoice date (client_ledger.txn_date of OV-526061 = 2026-07-07), duration fee_invoice_due_days 30 + late_charge_grace_days 10 -> start 2026-08-16, relation not_before, boundary exclusive; 2026-10-20 is later -> satisfied (just before: 2026-08-16 itself fails). The clause 'from then a charge of late_charge_pct_per_month percent of the unpaid invoice amount, and at least late_charge_minimum_usd, accrues once for each full calendar month the invoice stays unpaid.' is superseded by the extended sentence; the gate's condition sentence is untouched so the gate is inherited. Payment subject: same base policy, no gate applies (policy_scope). Placement hold: OV-526061 is the oldest unpaid invoice; its past-due limit 2026-10-05 passed, so the seeded hold of 2026-10-06 is the official state; after the payoff OV-526081 (due 2026-10-04) is still past due, so no resume is owed.
[Business-object card] Target object: invoice OV-526061 (2846.70). Rows entering: its invoice row, its 1010.00 part payment (2026-08-25), its late charge(s); excluded: payments and late charges carrying other invoice numbers (OV-525071/OV-525101/OV-526021 late charges count only as 'other invoices' in the minimum test), the reversed-collection credit on OV-526081. Windows: other-invoice late charges in 12 months (2026-01-16, 2026-05-14 in; 2025-10-15 out: MONTHS = 12), fee payments in 6 months = 6, collections in 3 months = 8260.00 (2026-07-14 out), returned payments in 3 months = 1, suits filed in 12 months = 2 (2025-09-18 out).
[Factor card — late charge, 6 factors (1 method, 5 parameter); baseline 1836.70 x 1.5% = 27.55 (greater of that and 5.00)] (1) precollect_payment_rate, parameter, cross-difficulty flatfee, multi-source (paid within invoice-due days AND pack age): -0.50 pt / -0.25 pt / tier rate; taken -0.50 (paid in 23 of 30 days, 19 months old) -> 1.00; substitution 24.14. (2) invoice_aging_step, parameter: >=150 days +0.50, 100-149 +0.25, else 0; taken +0.25 (105 days); substitution 15.19. (3) minimum_combination, method: >=2 other-invoice late charges in 12 months -> percentage plus minimum; none -> percentage alone; exactly one -> greater of; taken plus-minimum (2); substitution 14.92; near-miss: the 2025-10-15 charge on OV-525071 is 12 months and 5 days old and stays outside the 12-month window, and OV-526061's own 2026-09-16 charge is excluded as not an 'other' invoice — counting it would still land on the same tier but would mislead a reader of the payment-record and inclusion tests. Other near-misses: the invoice is 105 days old (5 days past the 100-day step), the 2026-07-14 collection falls just outside the 3-month window, the 2025-09-18 suit outside 12 months. (4) part_payment_relief: >=50% paid 25%, 25-49% 10%, else 0; taken 10% (35%); substitution 20.97. (5) tenure_relief: >=36 months 15%, 18-35 5%, else 0; taken 15% (41 months); substitution 22.37. (6) legal_standing_adjustment, cross-difficulty legal, multi-source (status AND deposit vs programme minimum): +10% relief / -10% surcharge (suspended and short) / 0; taken relief (active, 1315.00 >= 1000.00); substitution 20.97. Result 27.95875 x (1-0.35) = 18.17. History check: every earlier seeded late charge equals this rule at its own date (17.16, 20.53, 14.91, 15.19).
[Factor card — payoff, 5 factors (1 method, 4 parameter); baseline 1836.70 + 33.36 = 1870.06] (1) late_charge_inclusion, method, multi-source (days since latest charge AND count): within 10 days & <=3 charges -> latest only; within 10 days & >3 -> last 3 months' charges; else all; taken latest only (0 days, 2 charges); substitution 1845.04. (2) payment_record_concession: >=4 payments in 6 months 50%, 1-3 25%, none 0; taken 50% (6); substitution 1850.33. (3) legal_volume_concession, cross-difficulty legal: >=3 suits 25%, 1-2 10%, none 0; taken 10%; substitution 1843.06. (4) collection_volume_concession: >=10000 20%, 4000-9999.99 10%, else 0; taken 10% (8260.00); substitution 1843.06. (5) returned_payment_concession: >=2 10%, exactly 1 5%, none 0; taken 5%; substitution 1842.15. Result 1836.70 + 18.17 x 0.25 = 1841.24.
[Rule <-> compute sweep] Forward: every reading/branching binding quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis (unpaid amount definition, pack test, aging step, minimum combination, three reliefs, combination 'first added into one share ... reduced once', rounding once at the end; inclusion ladder, four concession ladders, 'never more than the whole' (MN 1), 'the unpaid amount itself is never reduced'). Reverse: the invoice is located as the invoice of the agreement's most recent late charge (the invoice whose monthly charges are accruing; at both handling times it is OV-526061); 'never less than zero' -> MX(0, ...). Known limit recorded for audit: the compute locates the invoice by the latest late charge, which coincides with the invoice being charged whenever that invoice already accrues charges, as here.
[Seed] SEED-FRESH: 1 creditor client, 1 Preferred agreement (placement_hold fees_past_due), 71 client ledger rows for periods Jul 2025-Sep 2026 plus the October collection (earlier periods fully settled, netting to zero), legal agreement Client-Advanced (deposit 2500.00 - 3 x 395.00 applied = 1315.00, advance 0) with 16 matter rows, flatfee 300-unit program with its purchase entry. Automatic clauses: all closed periods remitted within SLA and invoiced within 5 business days; the only returned payment carries its credit; OV-526081 starts accruing late charges 2026-10-14 but completes no full month before 2026-11-14; OV-526091 not due; no other invoice owes a late charge; tier review 2027-05-01; term renews 2027-04-30.
[Persona] Ignatius Feldmann-Okafor, collections manager, formal and methodical; volunteers the invoice number OV-526061 and the wish to pay it off himself; phone 5745555816 and EIN last four 5947 only on request; says other invoices are not part of today's call; agrees in one line if told something must be added first; pays exactly the quoted amount; notes the confirmation and ends.
[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, EIN last4) -> find_client_agreements -> find_client_ledger -> find_flatfee_programs -> find_flatfee_unit_ledger -> find_legal_agreements -> find_legal_matter_events -> unlock+call assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6(agreement, OV-526061, 18.17) -> unlock_user + call_user pay_past_due_invoice_8492adb5(agreement, OV-526061, 1841.24).
[Verification run] /tmp harness, real tools, handling-time snapshots: late charge 18.17 (branches 21), sensitivities {rate 24.14, aging 15.19, minimum 14.92, part-payment 20.97, tenure 22.37, legal 20.97}, baseline 27.55; payoff 1841.24 (branches 13), sensitivities {inclusion 1845.04, payment record 1850.33, legal 1843.06, volume 1843.06, returned 1842.15}, baseline 1870.06; skipping the late charge -> payoff 1840.50. Gates --task 1: extended, task tools, replay, solvability, compute, grounding all OK.
[Revisions] (1) 2026-08-26 collection fell in August's last 5 business days (clearance roll-forward) -> moved to 2026-08-19. (2) A placement-hold-based concession would have sat on its fall-through on this held agreement -> replaced by a payment-record concession on fee payments in 6 months; rule, compute, basis and factor updated together.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules, schemas, finder returns and persona: the caller wants OV-526061 paid off; the payoff rule waits on a late charge for every full month after the start; the ledger shows one of two; the late-charge rule yields 18.17; the payoff rule yields 1841.24 with only the latest charge entering. Matches gold; no alternative reading found (tiers are worded disjoint with explicit 'less than' bounds).
[Rework r2 — policy-task audit r1 (task 1 PASS; observations)]
1-O1 change: the late-charge and payoff rules now define the month: 'A full calendar month after a late-charge start runs from that day to the same day of the next month, or to that month's last day where the same day does not exist.' — matching the ledger precedent (every seeded charge one month after its start) and closing the calendar-month reading.
1-O2 response: the late-charge computation's tier-moving near-miss is the aging anchor: the rule counts from the invoice date (105 days -> +0.25); a reader anchoring on the due date (75 days) or the late-charge start (65 days) falls below the 100-day step and drops the step. Rule-excluded records also present: the 2025-10-15 other-invoice charge (12 months 5 days back) and the same-invoice 2026-09-16 charge. The payoff keeps its tier-moving near-misses (2026-07-14 collection, 2025-09-18 suit).
1-O3 / D8 change: two declared substitution figures sat on half-cent ties. The OV-526061 part payment was set to 1010.00 (share 35.5 percent, same tier) and its 2026-09-16 charge re-figured under the rule at that date to 15.19 (1836.70 x 1.00% + 5.00 = 23.367 x 0.65 = 15.18855); fees_receivable 3336.15 -> 3326.09. New figures: late charge 18.17 (27.95875 x 0.65), sensitivities rate 24.14, aging 15.19, minimum 14.92, part-payment 20.97, tenure 22.37, legal 20.97, baseline 27.55; payoff 1841.24 (1836.70 + 18.17 x 0.25 = 1841.2425), sensitivities inclusion 1845.04, payment record 1850.33, legal 1843.06, volume 1843.06, returned 1842.15, baseline 1870.06; skipped prerequisite 1840.50. No gold or declared figure now sits on a tie. Tool docstrings now say 'rounded to the nearest cent (2 decimal places)' instead of 'half-up'.
Charter-level r2 items affecting this task: D2 payoff suit count scoped to the legal agreement naming this agreement and the late charge's flatfee reads filtered by agreement (one legal agreement, one program here: counts unchanged); D1 payoff scoped to agreements with no termination notice (none here); D6 the invoice locator (latest late charge's invoice) still coincides with OV-526061 at both handling times; recorded as an accepted limitation of the DSL, which cannot receive the invoice the client names. Re-ran all per-task gates green.
user_scenario: You are Ignatius Feldmann-Okafor, collections manager at Ostrander Valley Auto Credit, Inc., an auto finance company in Elkhart, Indiana that places its deficiency balances with Ridgeline Recovery Associates. You are calm and methodical, a little formal, and you like to have a reference number for everything. Ridgeline's past-due reminder is sitting on your desk for invoice OV-526061, the fee invoice for June; your company sent part of it, a little over a thousand dollars, back in August, and accounts payable has now released the funds for the rest. You are calling to pay off invoice OV-526061 in full today, and you will make the payment yourself on this call. You open by saying who you are, which company you are with, and that you want to pay off invoice OV-526061 completely. You do not know the exact remaining amount and you ask the representative to tell you what it takes to clear that invoice. You give identifying details only when asked: the collections line on file is 5745555816 and the last four digits of the company's EIN are 5947; if asked for the company name you say Ostrander Valley Auto Credit, Inc. If asked about the earlier payment, you say you remember a little over a thousand dollars went out in late August but you do not have the exact date in front of you. If the representative asks about other invoices, you say that today you are only paying OV-526061 and the others are still going through approval on your side. If asked about your legal forwarding or your pre-collect letter program, you say nothing about them is changing today. If the representative tells you something needs to be added to the invoice before the payoff can be given, you say that is understood and they may go ahead; you only want the right figure. When the representative gives you the payoff amount and hands the payment over to you, you pay invoice OV-526061 yourself for exactly that amount. You do not dispute the figure, offer a number of your own, or comment on how it was worked out. Once the payment confirmation comes back, you note the confirmation reference aloud, thank the representative and say goodbye.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: Value: the agreement reference returned by find_client_agreements (the client's only agreement). Basis: docstring 'the placement agreement reference number (agreement id) of the agreement the invoice was raised on, read from the placement agreement lookup'. Uniqueness: invoice OV-526061 sits on this agreement's money history.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_number: Value: OV-526061. Basis: the caller's line 'invoice OV-526061' and the invoice entry in find_client_ledger; the late-charge rule figures 'Each monthly late charge on a past-due fee invoice'. Uniqueness: it is the past-due invoice whose second full month after its 2026-08-16 late-charge start ended 2026-10-16 with no charge booked; OV-526081 (due 2026-10-04, start 2026-10-14) has not completed a full month and OV-526091 is not due.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.late_charge_amount: Value: 18.17. Factors: unpaid 2846.70-1010.00 = 1836.70; (1) precollect_payment_rate — pack bought 2025-03-04, paid 2025-03-27 (23 <= 30 days), 19 months old -> 1.5 - 0.50 = 1.00 percent; (2) invoice_aging_step — 105 days since 2026-07-07 (>=100, <150) -> +0.25 -> 1.25 percent; percentage charge 22.95875; (3) minimum_combination — 2 late charges on other invoices in 12 months (2026-01-16, 2026-05-14; 2025-10-15 falls outside) -> percentage plus the 5.00 minimum = 27.95875; (4) part_payment_relief — 1010/2846.70 = 35.5 percent paid -> 10 percent; (5) tenure_relief — 41 months -> 15 percent; (6) legal_standing_adjustment — legal agreement active, deposit 1315.00 >= 1000.00 -> 10 percent; share 0.35 applied once: 27.95875 x 0.65 = 18.173 -> 18.17 (baseline 27.55).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the client's invoice payoff tool so the caller can pay himself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The client pays off invoice OV-526061 with 1841.24.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: client_ext_past_due_invoice_payoff computes payment_amount after the late charge is booked; it is the root problem the caller asked for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: Value: the same agreement reference from find_client_agreements. Basis: docstring 'the agreement the invoice belongs to, which the representative reads from the placement agreement lookup and gives to the client'. Uniqueness: one agreement.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_number: Value: OV-526061. Basis: the caller names it ('invoice OV-526061'); docstring 'the fee invoice number the client names for the payment ... (verbatim)'. Uniqueness: the only invoice the caller asks to pay.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_amount: Value: 1841.24. Factors after the 18.17 booking: unpaid 1836.70; (1) late_charge_inclusion — paid 0 days after the most recent late charge, invoice carries 2 late charges (<=3) -> only the latest 18.17 enters (baseline: both, 33.36); (2) payment_record_concession — 6 fee payments in 6 months -> 50 percent; (3) legal_volume_concession — 2 suits filed in 12 months -> 10 percent; (4) collection_volume_concession — collections in 3 months 8260.00 (>=4000, <10000) -> 10 percent; (5) returned_payment_concession — one returned-payment reversal (2026-09-08) in 3 months -> 5 percent; concession share 0.75: 18.17 x 0.25 = 4.5425; payoff = 1836.70 + 4.5425 = 1841.2425 -> 1841.24 (baseline 1870.06).

invoice_aging_step (parameter): OV-526061 dated 2026-07-07 is 105 days old (>=100, <150) -> +0.25; baseline 0 -> result 15.19.

part_payment_relief (parameter): 1010.00 paid of 2846.70 = 35.5 percent (>=25, <50) -> 10 percent; baseline 0 -> result 20.97.
tenure_relief (parameter): 41 whole months since 2023-05-01 -> 15 percent; baseline 0 -> result 22.37.

legal_standing_adjustment (parameter, cross-difficulty legal, multi-source): Client-Advanced legal agreement active, deposit 1315.00 >= programme minimum 1000.00 -> 10 percent relief; baseline 0 -> result 20.97.
plumbing: lc_invoice = OV-526061 (invoice of the latest late charge); unpaid 1836.70; monthly rate 1.25; percentage charge 22.95875; relief share 0.35; result RND(27.95875 x 0.65) = 18.17.

payments are at least a quarter but less than half of the invoice amount
36 or more whole months since the agreement's effective date
the legal agreement is active and its cost deposit is at or above the programme minimum

returned_payment_concession (parameter): one returned-payment reversal (2026-09-08) in 3 months -> 5 percent; baseline 0 -> result 1842.15.

4 or more fee payments in the 6 months before the payoff

edges.condition: The client money history carries, for the invoice being paid off, one late-charge entry for each full calendar month elapsed since its late-charge start (invoice date plus the due days plus the grace days), the latest month included.
edges.policy_source: A payoff figure for a past-due invoice is not quoted until the invoice carries a late charge for every full calendar month it has stayed unpaid after its late-charge start.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: OV-526061 is dated 2026-07-07; with 30 due days and 10 grace days its late-charge start is 2026-08-16, so two full months (to 2026-09-16 and to 2026-10-16) have passed by 2026-10-20, but only one late charge (2026-09-16, 15.19) is booked on it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6 books the second month's 18.17 charge on OV-526061; the invoice's most recent late charge becomes 18.17 dated 2026-10-20 and late_entering changes from 15.19 to 18.17.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, a chain: the missing month's late charge must be booked before the payoff is quoted ('A payoff figure for a past-due invoice is not quoted until the invoice carries a late charge for every full calendar month it has stayed unpaid after its late-charge start.'); no parallel prerequisites.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late-charge booking: no 2026-10-20 late-charge row on OV-526061, the most recent charge is the 2026-09-16 one (34 days old) so every charge (15.19) enters, and the payoff recomputes to 1840.50 instead of 1841.24; fees_receivable ends 1485.59 instead of 1503.02.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay off invoice OV-526061 in full; it never mentions a late charge being missing, a month's charge, or anything to be booked first, and the caller reacts only after the representative explains.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: pay_past_due_invoice_8492adb5 records the payment and lowers fees_receivable without checking late charges; assess_invoice_late_charge_7a6464d6 books the charge without checking dates or amounts. Neither returns an error or hint.

request_alignment.claim: The client wants to pay off one named past-due fee invoice in full today and will pay it himself.
evidence: user_scenario:You are calling to pay off invoice OV-526061 in full today, and you will make the payment yourself on this call.

gold_actions.business_effect: Books the second full month's late charge (18.17) on invoice OV-526061.

request_binding.action_semantics: The invoice's late-charge start passed on 2026-08-16 and a second full month ended 2026-10-16 with no charge booked, so a late charge is owed (state_due) and the payoff the client asked for is not quoted until it stands; a credit, a recall fee or a hold change would not bring that state about.

discriminator.business_meaning: a month's late charge owed on a past-due fee invoice

stage_provenance.fact: The late charge is booked synchronously by this call on the invoice already past due before the call.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A late charge accrues on an unpaid invoice only when the handling date is later than the late-charge start counted from the invoice date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The late-charge start is the invoice date plus fee_invoice_due_days calendar days plus late_charge_grace_days calendar days; from then a charge of late_charge_pct_per_month percent of the unpaid invoice amount, and at least late_charge_minimum_usd, accrues once for each full calendar month the invoice stays unpaid.

boundary_check.just_before: Late-charge start = 2026-07-07 + 30 + 10 = 2026-08-16; on 2026-08-16 itself the handling date is not later than the start, so no charge could accrue (exclusive boundary).
boundary_check.at_boundary: From 2026-08-17 a charge may accrue; one accrues for each full calendar month unpaid, the second month ending 2026-10-16, so on 2026-10-20 the second month's charge is owed.
